title: December, 2019
venue: Arthur's site · the coastal weeklies · the aggregator
logline: Does Chloe come home. She does. To the garage. She sits in the chair — his chair — and reads the whole year off the wall.

panels.composition: The garage. CHLOE in Wood's drafting chair, the swing-arm lamp on her, reading the pages pinned around the wall. WOOD on the floor with BARNABY II. The reversal is the panel.

characters.pose: in his chair, reading the wall
on the floor with the dog

image.prompt: a woman with pinned dark hair sitting in a cartoonist's drafting chair under a green swing-arm lamp reading the comic pages pinned all around a garage wall, the cartoonist sitting on the floor with a three-legged dog, razor-sharp ink

balloons.text: You drew the lockbox on my parents' door.
You stopped one panel longer than a stranger would.
I count everything. Since the cafeteria.

image.prompt: close-up of a woman reading comic pages on a wall with a level expression, speaking without turning

panels.composition: Chloe turning the chair to face him. The lamp behind her now.

balloons.text: Julian and I are done. Not yet. But done.

image.prompt: a woman turning a drafting chair to face a man sitting on the floor, the lamp behind her, a dog between them

panels.composition: The garage from the door. Her in his chair. Him on the floor. The pup. The lamp. Neither moving. The strip's Christmas.

image.prompt: a garage studio from its doorway at night: a woman in the drafting chair under the lamp, a man on the floor, a three-legged dog, pages on every wall, no words

art.line: razor-sharp brush and ink; Sundays wet-on-wet; 2019: the Sunday drawn to a smaller grid
art.palette: ink and one tone; Sundays gray-green, fog, rust; 2020: ochre and slate arriving

notes: She reads the year off the wall. 'Done. Not yet. But done.' Her in his chair.
